column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|04-08|2013|Μάργκαρετ Θάτσερ|Margaret Thatcher|Margaret Thatcher was a British Conservative politician. She was the first woman prime minister of the United Kingdom, from 1979 to 1990. She pursued a policy of privatisation and restriction of the trade unions, and she led the country in the Falklands War. She was nicknamed the "Iron Lady".

bio|04-09|1336|Ταμερλάνος|Timur|Timur was born near Samarkand. He was a conqueror from Central Asia who built a great empire. He defeated the Ottoman sultan Bayezid at the Battle of Ankara in 1402 and died in 1405.

bio|04-09|1553|Φρανσουά Ραμπελαί|Francois Rabelais|Francois Rabelais was a French writer, doctor and former monk. He wrote the satirical and humorous novels "Gargantua" and "Pantagruel", with rich language and criticism of his age.

bio|04-09|1626|Σερ Φράνσις Μπέικον|Francis Bacon|Sir Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and politician. In "Novum Organum" he argued for inductive method and for observation as the basis of science. He was Lord Chancellor and died in 1626, according to tradition after an experiment with snow.

bio|04-09|1821|Σαρλ Μπωντλέρ|Charles Baudelaire|Charles Baudelaire was a French poet. He wrote the collection "The Flowers of Evil", which caused a scandal in 1857 and influenced symbolism and later poetry. He also translated Edgar Allan Poe.

bio|04-09|1835|Λεοπόλδος Β΄|Leopold II|Leopold II was king of Belgium from 1865 to 1909. He founded the "Congo Free State" as his personal possession, where serious violence was committed against the population.

bio|04-09|1882|Ντάντε Γκάμπριελ Ροσέτι|Dante Gabriel Rossetti|Dante Gabriel Rossetti was an English poet and painter. He founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood and painted works such as "Beata Beatrix". He also wrote poetry, such as "The House of Life".

bio|04-09|1933|Ζαν Πολ Μπελμοντό|Jean-Paul Belmondo|Jean-Paul Belmondo was a French actor. He became a symbol of the French "New Wave" with Godard's "Breathless" and appeared in many French action and comedy films.

bio|04-09|1959|Φρανκ Λόιντ Ράιτ|Frank Lloyd Wright|Frank Lloyd Wright was an American architect. He developed "organic architecture" and designed Fallingwater and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York. He died in 1959.

bio|04-09|1990|Κρίστεν Στιούαρτ|Kristen Stewart|Kristen Stewart is an American actress. She became known for the "Twilight" films and was nominated for an Oscar for her performance as Princess Diana in "Spencer".

bio|04-10|1583|Ούγκο Γκρότιους|Hugo Grotius|Hugo Grotius was a Dutch jurist and philosopher. He is regarded as one of the founders of international law. In "On the Law of War and Peace" he set out basic principles on the rights of states.

bio|04-10|1755|Σάμουελ Χάνεμαν|Samuel Hahnemann|Samuel Hahnemann was a German doctor and the founder of homeopathy, an alternative method of treatment based on the theory of "like cures like". The method has no scientific support.

bio|04-10|1813|Ζοζέφ Λουί Λαγκράνζ|Joseph-Louis Lagrange|Joseph-Louis Lagrange was born in Turin and lived in Berlin and Paris. He was a mathematician and astronomer and contributed to analytical mechanics, number theory and the calculus of variations.

bio|04-10|1847|Τζόζεφ Πούλιτζερ|Joseph Pulitzer|Joseph Pulitzer was born in Hungary and emigrated to the United States. He was a journalist and publisher of the newspapers St. Louis Post-Dispatch and New York World. With his will the Pulitzer Prizes were established.

bio|04-10|1919|Εμιλιάνο Ζαπάτα|Emiliano Zapata|Emiliano Zapata was a Mexican farmer and a leader of the Mexican Revolution. He led the Liberation Army of the South and demanded the distribution of land to the farmers under the slogan "Land and Liberty". He was murdered in 1919.

bio|04-10|1931|Χαλίλ Γκιμπράν|Khalil Gibran|Khalil Gibran was a Lebanese poet and painter who lived in the United States. He wrote in English the book "The Prophet", which is one of the most popular books in the world. He died in New York in 1931.
bio|04-10|1932|Ομάρ Σαρίφ|Omar Sharif|Omar Sharif was an Egyptian actor. He became internationally known for the films "Lawrence of Arabia" and "Doctor Zhivago". He died in 2015.

bio|04-10|1973|Ρομπέρτο Κάρλος|Roberto Carlos|Roberto Carlos is a former Brazilian footballer. He played as a left-back for Real Madrid and Brazil and won the World Cup of 2002. He was known for his powerful shots and for the free kick goal of 1997, struck with a swerving run-up.

bio|04-10|2010|Λεχ Κατσίνσκι|Lech Kaczynski|Lech Kaczynski was a Polish politician. He was mayor of Warsaw and from 2005 president of Poland. He was killed in 2010 in an air crash near Smolensk in Russia, together with many state officials.

bio|04-11|146|Σεπτίμιος Σεβήρος|Septimius Severus|Septimius Severus was born in Leptis Magna in North Africa and became a Roman emperor in 193. He founded the Severan dynasty and strengthened the army. He died in Britain in 211.

bio|04-11|1492|Μαργαρίτα|Margaret of Navarre|Margaret of Navarre, also known as Margaret of Angouleme, was queen of Navarre and a writer. She wrote the "Heptameron", a collection of short stories. She was the sister of Francis I of France and a patron of the humanists.

bio|04-11|1770|Τζωρτζ Κάνινγκ|George Canning|George Canning was a British politician. He was foreign secretary and prime minister for a few months in 1827. He supported the Greek Revolution and prepared the London Protocol of 1826.

bio|04-11|1953|Άντριου Γουάιλς|Andrew Wiles|Andrew Wiles is a British mathematician. In 1994 he proved Fermat's Last Theorem, a problem that had remained unsolved for 350 years. In 2016 he was awarded the Abel Prize.

bio|04-11|1985|Ενβέρ Χότζα|Enver Hoxha|Enver Hoxha was an Albanian communist politician. He ruled Albania from 1944 until his death with an authoritarian and isolated regime, and he banned religion. He died in 1985.
bio|04-11|1987|Πρίμο Λέβι|Primo Levi|Primo Levi was an Italian chemist and writer of Jewish origin. He survived Auschwitz and wrote the book "If This Is a Man". He died in Turin in 1987.

bio|04-11|2007|Κουρτ Βόνεγκατ|Kurt Vonnegut|Kurt Vonnegut was an American writer. He wrote the novel "Slaughterhouse-Five" about the bombing of Dresden, with elements of science fiction and black humour. He died in 2007.

bio|04-11|2012|Αχμέντ Μπεν Μπελά|Ahmed Ben Bella|Ahmed Ben Bella was an Algerian politician. He was the leader of the struggle for independence from France and the first president of Algeria, from 1963 to 1965, when he was overthrown.

bio|04-12|1555|Ιωάννα Α΄|Joanna I of Castile|Joanna I of Castile, known as "the Mad", was queen of Castile and the mother of the emperor Charles V. Because she was considered mentally unstable, her father and then her son imprisoned her and governed in her name.

bio|04-12|1817|Σαρλ Μεσιέ|Charles Messier|Charles Messier was a French astronomer and comet hunter. He created the Messier catalogue, with more than 100 nebulae and star clusters, such as the Andromeda Galaxy (M31), so that they would not be confused with comets.

bio|04-12|1933|Μονσεράτ Καμπαγιέ|Montserrat Caballe|Montserrat Caballe was a Spanish soprano from Catalonia. She excelled in the operas of Verdi and Donizetti, and in 1987 she sang the song "Barcelona" with Freddie Mercury.
bio|04-12|1942|Τζέικομπ Ζούμα|Jacob Zuma|Jacob Zuma is a South African politician. He was president of South Africa from 2009 to 2018, when he resigned after charges of corruption.

bio|04-12|1945|Φραγκλίνος Ρούζβελτ|Franklin D. Roosevelt|Franklin D. Roosevelt died on 12 April 1945 of a cerebral haemorrhage. He was the 32nd president of the United States and led the country through the Great Depression and the Second World War, for more than 12 years.
bio|04-12|1947|Τομ Κλάνσυ|Tom Clancy|Tom Clancy was an American writer. He wrote techno-thrillers, such as "The Hunt for Red October", on military action and espionage. He died in 2013.

bio|04-12|1961|Λίζα Τζέραρντ|Lisa Gerrard|Lisa Gerrard is an Australian singer and composer. She was a member of the group Dead Can Dance and composed music for films such as "Gladiator". She has a powerful and distinctive voice.

bio|04-12|1971|Ίγκορ Ταμ|Igor Tamm|Igor Tamm was a Russian physicist. Together with Frank and Cherenkov he explained the Cherenkov effect, and in 1958 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He also contributed to Soviet nuclear research.

bio|04-13|1695|Ζαν ντε Λα Φονταίν|Jean de La Fontaine|Jean de La Fontaine was a French poet. He wrote the "Fables", a collection of verse fables with animals, based partly on Aesop. He is one of the best-known French classical writers.

bio|04-13|1743|Τόμας Τζέφερσον|Thomas Jefferson|Thomas Jefferson was the 3rd president of the United States, from 1801 to 1809. He wrote the main part of the Declaration of Independence and was responsible for the Louisiana Purchase in 1803. He founded the University of Virginia.

bio|04-13|1906|Σάμιουελ Μπέκετ|Samuel Beckett|Samuel Beckett was an Irish writer who lived in France. He wrote the play "Waiting for Godot", one of the most important works of the theatre of the absurd. In 1969 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-13|1939|Σέιμους Χίνι|Seamus Heaney|Seamus Heaney was an Irish poet from Northern Ireland. He wrote poetry about the countryside and the conflict in his country, and he translated "Beowulf". In 1995 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-13|1940|Ζαν-Μαρί Γκυστάβ Λε Κλεζιό|J. M. G. Le Clezio|J. M. G. Le Clezio is a French writer. He has written novels and essays on migration and nature. In 2008 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-13|1956|Έμιλ Νόλντε|Emil Nolde|Emil Nolde was a German expressionist painter, born in what is now Denmark. He painted flowers and religious subjects in strong colours. The Nazis banned him as a "degenerate artist".

bio|04-13|1963|Γκάρι Κασπάροφ|Garry Kasparov|Garry Kasparov is a Russian chess player. He was world champion from 1985 to 2000 and is regarded as one of the greatest in history. In 1997 he lost a match to the computer Deep Blue. He later became involved in politics.

bio|04-13|2015|Γκύντερ Γκρας|Gunter Grass|Gunter Grass was a German writer. He wrote the novel "The Tin Drum". In 1999 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. In 2006 he revealed that he had served in the Waffen-SS.

bio|04-13|2015|Εδουάρδο Γκαλεάνο|Eduardo Galeano|Eduardo Galeano was a Uruguayan journalist and writer. He wrote "Open Veins of Latin America", about the exploitation of the continent, and "Soccer in Sun and Shadow".

bio|04-14|1126|Αβερρόης|Averroes|Averroes, that is Ibn Rushd, was born in Cordoba. He was an Arab philosopher, doctor and jurist, and he wrote extensive commentaries on the works of Aristotle. He had a significant influence on medieval thought in the West.

bio|04-14|1578|Φίλιππος Γ΄|Philip III|Philip III was king of Spain from 1598 to 1621. He left power to favourites, such as the Duke of Lerma. In 1609 he expelled the Moriscos, Muslims who had been baptised, from Spain.

bio|04-14|1629|Κρίστιαν Χόυχενς|Christiaan Huygens|Christiaan Huygens was a Dutch physicist and astronomer. He discovered Titan, a moon of Saturn, and its rings, invented the pendulum clock and formulated the wave theory of light.

bio|04-14|1759|Γκέοργκ Φρήντριχ Χαίντελ|George Frideric Handel|George Frideric Handel died in London in 1759. He was a German Baroque composer who lived in England and wrote "Messiah" and other oratorios, operas and works such as "Water Music".

bio|04-14|1917|Λουδοβίκος Λάζαρος Ζαμένχοφ|Ludwik Lazarus Zamenhof|Ludwik Lazarus Zamenhof was a Polish-Jewish eye doctor. In 1887 he created Esperanto, the international language, with the aim of communication between peoples. He died in Warsaw in 1917.

bio|04-14|1930|Βλαντίμιρ Μαγιακόφσκι|Vladimir Mayakovsky|Vladimir Mayakovsky was a Russian futurist poet. He supported the October Revolution and wrote poems and plays, such as "A Cloud in Trousers". He took his own life in 1930.
bio|04-14|1940|Τζούλι Κρίστι|Julie Christie|Julie Christie is an English actress. She won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Darling" and appeared in "Doctor Zhivago".

bio|04-14|1973|Έιντριεν Μπρόντι|Adrien Brody|Adrien Brody is an American actor. In 2003 he became the youngest person to win the Oscar for Best Actor, for Roman Polanski's "The Pianist". In 2025 he won a second Oscar for "The Brutalist".

bio|04-14|1986|Σιμόν ντε Μποβουάρ|Simone de Beauvoir|Simone de Beauvoir was a French philosopher and writer. She wrote "The Second Sex", a foundational work of feminism. She was the companion of Jean-Paul Sartre and died in 1986.

bio|04-15|1452|Λεονάρντο ντα Βίντσι|Leonardo da Vinci|Leonardo da Vinci was born in Vinci in Tuscany. He was a painter, inventor and scientist of the Renaissance. He painted the "Mona Lisa" and "The Last Supper", and left drawings of machines and anatomical studies.

bio|04-15|1707|Λέοναρντ Όιλερ|Leonhard Euler|Leonhard Euler was a Swiss mathematician and physicist. He contributed to many fields, such as calculus, graph theory and number theory, and introduced the notation for e and pi. He is one of the greatest mathematicians.

bio|04-15|1858|Εμίλ Ντιρκέμ|Emile Durkheim|Emile Durkheim was a French sociologist. He is regarded as one of the founders of sociology as a science. He wrote "Suicide" and "The Elementary Forms of Religious Life".

bio|04-15|1865|Αβραάμ Λίνκολν|Abraham Lincoln|Abraham Lincoln died on the morning of 15 April 1865, after being shot the previous evening at Ford's Theatre by John Wilkes Booth. He was the 16th president of the United States and had led the Union to victory in the Civil War.

bio|04-15|1894|Νικίτα Χρουστσόφ|Nikita Khrushchev|Nikita Khrushchev was a Soviet politician. He led the Soviet Union from 1953 to 1964. He condemned the crimes of Stalin and was a central figure in the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962.

bio|04-15|1912|Κιμ Ίλ-σονγκ|Kim Il-sung|Kim Il-sung was the founder and first leader of North Korea, from 1948 to 1994. He organised an authoritarian regime with a cult of personality. He was succeeded by his son Kim Jong Il.

bio|04-15|1980|Ζαν-Πωλ Σαρτρ|Jean-Paul Sartre|Jean-Paul Sartre was a French philosopher and writer and a leading representative of existentialism. He wrote "Being and Nothingness" and the novel "Nausea". In 1964 he refused the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-15|1990|Έμμα Γουάτσον|Emma Watson|Emma Watson is an English actress. She became known for the role of Hermione Granger in the "Harry Potter" films. She also appeared in "Little Women" and "Beauty and the Beast". She is a UN Goodwill Ambassador.

bio|04-15|1990|Γκρέτα Γκάρμπο|Greta Garbo|Greta Garbo was a Swedish actress and a major Hollywood star of the 1920s and 1930s. She appeared in "Anna Karenina" and "Ninotchka". She retired in 1941, at the age of 35, and lived in seclusion.

bio|04-15|1998|Πολ Ποτ|Pol Pot|Pol Pot was the leader of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia. From 1975 to 1979 he ruled the country with an extreme regime, which led to the deaths of about one to two million people. He died in 1998.

bio|04-16|1828|Φρανθίσκο Γκόγια|Francisco Goya|Francisco Goya died in Bordeaux, France, in 1828, where he had gone into exile. He was a Spanish painter and engraver who painted "The Third of May 1808" and the "Black Paintings".

bio|04-16|1844|Ανατόλ Φρανς|Anatole France|Anatole France was a French writer and critic. He wrote novels such as "The Crime of Sylvestre Bonnard" and "Penguin Island". In 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-16|1859|Αλεξίς ντε Τοκβίλ|Alexis de Tocqueville|Alexis de Tocqueville was a French historian and political thinker. He wrote "Democracy in America", an analysis of American society, and "The Old Regime and the Revolution". He died in 1859.

bio|04-16|1867|Γουίλμπουρ Ράιτ|Wilbur Wright|Wilbur Wright was an American aviation pioneer. Together with his brother Orville he made the first powered aircraft flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903. He died in 1912.

bio|04-16|1889|Τσάρλι Τσάπλιν|Charlie Chaplin|Charlie Chaplin was born in London and became an actor, director and composer of silent and sound cinema. He created the character of "the Tramp" and made films such as "The Kid", "City Lights" and "Modern Times".

bio|04-16|1940|Μαργαρίτα Β΄|Margrethe II|Margrethe II was queen of Denmark from 1972 to 2024, when she abdicated in favour of her son Frederik X. She was the first woman to reign in Denmark since the Middle Ages. She is also an artist.

bio|04-16|1958|Ρόζαλιντ Φράνκλιν|Rosalind Franklin|Rosalind Franklin was an English chemist and crystallographer. Using X-ray diffraction she took "Photo 51" of DNA, which helped Watson and Crick find its structure. She died young, of cancer, at the age of 37.
bio|04-16|1971|Selena|Selena|Selena Quintanilla was born in Texas and became known as the "Queen of Tejano music". She became famous in the 1990s and was murdered in 1995, at the age of 23.

bio|04-16|1972|Γιασουνάρι Καβαμπάτα|Yasunari Kawabata|Yasunari Kawabata was a Japanese writer. He wrote the novels "Snow Country" and "The Sound of the Mountain". In 1968 he became the first Japanese to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|04-17|1558|Χιουρέμ|Hurrem Sultan|Hurrem Sultan, also known as Roxelana, was the wife of the Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent. She had great influence at the court and died in 1558.

bio|04-17|1790|Βενιαμίν Φραγκλίνος|Benjamin Franklin|Benjamin Franklin died in Philadelphia in 1790. He was a printer, scientist, inventor and diplomat and one of the founders of the United States. He invented the lightning rod.

bio|04-17|1885|Ίσακ Ντίνεσεν|Isak Dinesen|Isak Dinesen, whose real name was Karen Blixen, was a Danish writer. She lived in Kenya and wrote "Out of Africa", which became a film. She also wrote short stories, such as "Babette's Feast".

bio|04-17|1897|Θόρντον Ουάιλντερ|Thornton Wilder|Thornton Wilder was an American novelist and playwright. He wrote the novel "The Bridge of San Luis Rey" and the play "Our Town". He won the Pulitzer Prize three times.

bio|04-17|1918|Γουίλιαμ Χόλντεν|William Holden|William Holden was an American actor. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "Stalag 17". He also appeared in "Sunset Boulevard" and "The Bridge on the River Kwai".

bio|04-17|1942|Ζαν Μπατίστ Περέν|Jean Perrin|Jean Perrin was a French physicist. He confirmed experimentally the existence of atoms and molecules by studying Brownian motion, and in 1926 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|04-17|1972|Τζένιφερ Γκάρνερ|Jennifer Garner|Jennifer Garner is an American actress. She became known through the television series "Alias" and appeared in films such as "Elektra" and "Daredevil".
bio|04-17|1992|Σκοντράν Μουσταφί|Skender Mustafi|Skender Mustafi is a German footballer of Albanian origin. He played as a defender for Valencia, Arsenal and the German national team.

bio|04-17|2014|Γκαμπριέλ Γκαρσία Μάρκες|Gabriel Garcia Marquez|Gabriel Garcia Marquez died in Mexico City in 2014. He was a Colombian writer, known for "One Hundred Years of Solitude" and "Love in the Time of Cholera". In 1982 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|04-18|1480|Λουκρητία Βοργία|Lucrezia Borgia|Lucrezia Borgia was the daughter of Pope Alexander VI. Her marriages served the political alliances of the family. As duchess of Ferrara she was a patron of the arts.

bio|04-18|1772|Ντέηβιντ Ρικάρντο|David Ricardo|David Ricardo was a British economist. He developed the theory of comparative advantage in international trade and wrote "On the Principles of Political Economy and Taxation".

bio|04-18|1802|Έρασμος Δαρβίνος|Erasmus Darwin|Erasmus Darwin was an English doctor, poet and naturalist, and the grandfather of Charles Darwin. He was a member of the Lunar Society and wrote "Zoonomia", with ideas about evolution.

bio|04-18|1927|Σάμιουελ Χάντιγκτον|Samuel Huntington|Samuel Huntington was an American political scientist. He wrote "The Clash of Civilizations", in which he argued that conflicts after the Cold War would be mainly cultural.
bio|04-18|1941|Μάικλ Ντ. Χίγκινς|Michael D. Higgins|Michael D. Higgins is an Irish politician and poet. He was president of Ireland from 2011. He has defended human rights and has published poetry.

bio|04-18|1943|Ισορόκου Γιαμαμότο|Isoroku Yamamoto|Isoroku Yamamoto was an admiral of the Imperial Japanese Navy and the planner of the attack on Pearl Harbor. His aircraft was shot down by American fighters in 1943, after interception of his messages.

bio|04-18|1955|Άλμπερτ Αϊνστάιν|Albert Einstein|Albert Einstein died on 18 April 1955 in Princeton, from a rupture of an aortic aneurysm. He was the physicist who developed the theory of relativity and had been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

bio|04-18|2002|Θορ Χέιερνταλ|Thor Heyerdahl|Thor Heyerdahl was a Norwegian explorer and anthropologist. In 1947 he crossed the Pacific on the raft "Kon-Tiki" to support his claim that ancient people of South America could have reached Polynesia.

bio|04-19|1824|Λόρδος Βύρων|Lord Byron|Lord Byron died in Missolonghi on 19 April 1824 of a fever. He was a British Romantic poet and a philhellene, who had come to Greece to help the Revolution. Greece regards him as a national benefactor.

bio|04-19|1881|Μπέντζαμιν Ντισραέλι|Benjamin Disraeli|Benjamin Disraeli was a British Conservative politician and writer. He was prime minister in 1868 and from 1874 to 1880. He bought the shares of the Suez Canal for Britain and proclaimed Queen Victoria Empress of India.

bio|04-19|1882|Κάρολος Δαρβίνος|Charles Darwin|Charles Darwin died in 1882 and was buried in Westminster Abbey. He was an English naturalist who formulated the theory of evolution by natural selection in "On the Origin of Species".

bio|04-19|1933|Τζέιν Μάνσφιλντ|Jayne Mansfield|Jayne Mansfield was an American actress and a sex symbol of the 1950s, who became known for her resemblance to Marilyn Monroe. She was killed in a car accident in 1967.

bio|04-19|1967|Κόνραντ Αντενάουερ|Konrad Adenauer|Konrad Adenauer died in 1967. He was the first chancellor of West Germany, from 1949 to 1963. He advocated reconciliation with France and membership of NATO.

bio|04-19|1968|Μσουάτι Γ΄|Mswati III|Mswati III has been king of Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, since 1986. He is an absolute monarch, and the country is one of the last absolute monarchies in Africa. In 2018 he changed the name of the country to Eswatini.
bio|04-19|1978|Τζέιμς Φράνκο|James Franco|James Franco is an American actor and director. He was nominated for an Oscar for "127 Hours" and played Harry Osborn in the "Spider-Man" film series.

bio|04-19|1979|Κέιτ Χάντσον|Kate Hudson|Kate Hudson is an American actress, the daughter of Goldie Hawn. She was nominated for the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "Almost Famous" and has appeared in romantic comedies such as "How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days".

bio|04-19|1987|Μαρία Σαράποβα|Maria Sharapova|Maria Sharapova is a former Russian tennis player. She won five Grand Slam tournaments, including Wimbledon in 2004 at the age of 17. In 2016 she was sanctioned for doping.

bio|04-20|1314|Πάπας Κλήμης Ε΄|Pope Clement V|Pope Clement V was pope from 1305 to 1314. He moved the seat of the papacy from Rome to Avignon in France, in the period of the "Avignon Papacy". During his time the Order of the Knights Templar was dissolved.

bio|04-20|1808|Ναπολέων Γ΄|Napoleon III|Napoleon III was the nephew of Napoleon I. He was elected president of France in 1848 and became emperor in 1852. He was defeated by Prussia at the Battle of Sedan in 1870.

bio|04-20|1889|Αδόλφος Χίτλερ|Adolf Hitler|Adolf Hitler was born in Austria. He was the leader of the Nazi Party and from 1933 the dictator of Germany. His aggressive policy caused the Second World War and the Holocaust. He took his own life in 1945.

bio|04-20|1893|Ζουάν Μιρό|Joan Miro|Joan Miro was a Spanish painter and sculptor from Catalonia, with a surrealist and playful style. His works use bright colours and symbolic shapes, and a museum dedicated to him is in Barcelona.

bio|04-20|1912|Μπραμ Στόκερ|Bram Stoker|Bram Stoker was an Irish writer. He wrote the novel "Dracula" in 1897, which became a landmark of horror literature. He was also the manager of the Lyceum Theatre in London.

bio|04-20|1918|Καρλ Φέρντιναντ Μπράουν|Karl Ferdinand Braun|Karl Ferdinand Braun was a German physicist. He developed the cathode-ray tube, and in 1909 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Marconi for his contribution to wireless telegraphy.

bio|04-20|1949|Τζέσικα Λανγκ|Jessica Lange|Jessica Lange is an American actress. She won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "Tootsie" and the Oscar for Best Actress for "Blue Sky". She also appeared in "King Kong" and the series "American Horror Story".

bio|04-20|1960|Μιγκέλ Ντίας-Κανέλ|Miguel Diaz-Canel|Miguel Diaz-Canel is a Cuban politician. He succeeded Raul Castro and became president of Cuba in 2018. Since 2021 he has also been the first secretary of the Communist Party.

bio|04-20|2018|Avicii|Avicii|Avicii, whose real name was Tim Bergling, was a Swedish DJ and electronic music producer. He became famous with "Wake Me Up" and "Levels". He died in 2018, at the age of 28.

bio|04-21|1699|Ρακίνας|Jean Racine|Jean Racine was a French playwright. He wrote tragedies such as "Phaedra", "Andromache" and "Iphigenia", with themes from Greek mythology and in a classical style. He died in 1699.

bio|04-21|1816|Σαρλότ Μπροντέ|Charlotte Bronte|Charlotte Bronte was born in Yorkshire and became a writer. She wrote the novel "Jane Eyre". She was the sister of Emily and Anne Bronte and died in 1855.

bio|04-21|1864|Μαξ Βέμπερ|Max Weber|Max Weber was a German sociologist and economist. He wrote "The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism" and developed concepts for bureaucracy and authority.
